changelogs.description:
Use the SGLang ROCm 7.2.0 MI35x 20261113 daily image (lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.23-rocm720-mi35x-20261113, SGLang 0.5.23.dev20261113+g5792cf6e5e) for GLM-5.2 MXFP4 MI355X AgentX MTP.
Use Gluon target MoE only for TP8/EP1 at concurrency 1 and 2; preserve the checkpoint BF16 draft experts with the auto speculative MoE backend.
TP8/EP1 keeps 32k prefill chunks; the image includes the Gluon FP32 partial-store fix from sgl-project/sglang#48397.
Drop the TP8/EP1 concurrency 4 point; concurrency 4 runs on the TP4/EP4 HiCache arm, which delivers more throughput per GPU.
Keep TP4/EP4 HiCache and DCP4 settings unchanged and run GSM8K on every eval-selected point, including the Gluon path.

Keep the lmsysorg/sglang:dev-kimi-k31-pro image (same digest) and the RadixArk/Kimi-K3.1-Dflash2-Preview DFLASH draft; only the search space changes.
Add 3P1D c224: three TP8/DCP8 EP2 prefill workers and one TP32 decode worker (DCP8 x attention DP4, EP32 MegaMoE) on 8 nodes, verifying 8 tokens. It replaces 1P1D c60.
Run 1P3D (TP8 decode) at c58 instead of c50, with the same recipe.
Aggregated megakernel c4 sets 11 K31MK_* schedule options instead of 15: drop K31MK_EXPERTS_COOPERATIVE, K31MK_KDA_TOKEN_OWNED, K31MK_OPROJ_NORM_FOLD and K31MK_TAIL_RMS_FOLD.
4P1D c520, 3P1D c340, 2P1D c180, 1P4D c36 and c16, and megakernel c2 are unchanged.

Add GLM-5.3 MXFP4 MI355X AgentX on SGLang (amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8) with EAGLE MTP K5 and golden AL 3.48, on lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261025 pinned by digest; the v0.5.22 release lacks sgl-project/sglang#40776, which this checkpoint needs to load.
TP4/EP4 with a 180 GB/rank write-back HiCache host tier and breakable prefill CUDA graphs at concurrency 4, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16 and 20; TP8/EP1 without KV offloading at concurrency 1, 2 and 4. On both arms, max-running-requests and the decode CUDA graph limit are twice the concurrency.
Every rank runs the Python TreeCore (SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python): ranks otherwise pick the Rust or Python core on their own, and mixed cores fail the write-back HiCache sync assertion (sgl-project/sglang#48112).
Draft data types: the NextN layer shipped in the checkpoint loads with its Quark config, as shipped (MXFP4 routed and shared experts, FP8 per-block attention and indexer wq_b/wk, BF16 eh_proj, router gate and indexer weights_proj).

New key on vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-60bd6dd2edd175a1c55fd3488f871e4c3d2ef27d (2026-11-16, digest sha256:67a3a0fb79893fc5a0fcff5f9b739ba8fec7e920875a12e0574c2e9f50cd814c), which carries vllm-project/vllm#64715 (UMBP standalone mode for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on ROCm), #66036 (per-tensor fp8_e4m3 KV cache for sparse MLA on ROCm) and #67377 (AITER FlyDSL dense MXFP8 GEMMs and a faster MXFP8 activation quant for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). Its MORI v1.2.3.post1 is built with UMBP. The TP4/TP2 key dsv41flash-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-dspark and the TP8 c1 key are unchanged and are not rerun.
Add concurrency 128, 256 and 384 on two GPUs with attention DP2 and the MoE tensor-parallel across both ranks (tensor-parallel-size 1, data-parallel-size 2, no expert parallelism), fronted by vllm-router 0.1.14 with consistent_hash: prefill cadence (prefill-schedule-interval 11), no --monokernel, five-token DSpark, block size 128, the MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer, Engram tables in host memory, max-num-batched-tokens 16384 and cudagraph capture up to 1024. Concurrency 128 runs without KV offloading, as in the closed https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4992, because the GPU KV cache holds its working set; 256 and 384 add UMBP.
At 256 and 384, KV offloading to host DRAM through UMBPStoreConnector in standalone mode: a node-local umbp_standalone_server, launched as a critical srt-slurm service before the workers, owns one 449 GB pool (dram-utilization 0.60 of the two-GPU share, 4 KiB pages) shared by both DP ranks; failed loads are recomputed.
kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 (vllm-project/vllm#66036) at every point: plain per-tensor fp8 KV rows read by the AITER sparse MLA kernel, instead of the default block-scaled fp8_ds_mla record.
Draft weights unchanged: the DSpark draft (mtp.0-2 in the target checkpoint) loads with the checkpoint's FP8 config, as shipped. Its attention layers share the target's KV cache dtype, so target and draft both use the per-tensor fp8_e4m3 KV cache.

Update to vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8ca766326652caf4b8e50d1b9118d8a22f6adc73, which selects FlashInfer's SM90 MSA kernels for the indexer and sparse attention.
Serve flags, DSpark speculation and the search space are unchanged.
